answer: Bind each identity to a latency fingerprint measured from five far beacons: every epoch the network pings the agent's endpoint and records the ridge of round-trip times, a profile stable for one machine but nearly impossible to fake for many. A voyage of clones behind one router shares one delta of delays, so their fingerprints collapse into a single cluster and only one of them counts. To pass as a thousand, a farm must rent a thousand geographically separate machines with distinct paths, paying real hosting per head, while an honest agent's single fingerprint costs nothing to keep.
